source_paper_text:
For nonnegative integers m,r define S_r^(m)(x)=sum_{i=0}^r sum_{j=0}^r binom(r,i)^m binom(r,j)^m binom(i+j,i) x^(i+j). Binomial coefficients have their ordinary factorial definition. Write S_r(x)=S_r^(2)(x). For an odd prime p, (a/p) is the Legendre symbol: zero if p divides a, one for a nonzero quadratic residue modulo p, and minus one otherwise. Rational congruence a=b mod p^2 means v_p(a-b)>=2; a rational number belongs to Z_p precisely when its reduced denominator is coprime to p. For a sequence (P_r(q)) indexed by r>=a, q-log-convexity means every coefficient of P_(r-1)(q)P_(r+1)(q)-P_r(q)^2 is nonnegative at each r>=a+1. Define U_r(q)=sum_{j=0}^r binom(r,j)^3 q^j and V_r,m(q)=sum_{j=0}^r binom(r+j,j)^m q^j.

Faithful mathematical restatement of Conjecture 1.1 (both parts):
All four assertions hold: (U_r(q))_(r>=8) is q-log-convex; for every integer m>=2, (V_r,m(q))_(r>=0) is q-log-convex; (S_r^(2)(q))_(r>=0) is q-log-convex; and (S_r^(3)(q))_(r>=2) is q-log-convex. Equivalently, the central-index ranges are r>=9, r>=1, r>=1, and r>=3 respectively.
